assumptions: The link between the flag rollout and the failures is inferred from timing and log correlation (errors appear in the same minute the flag reaches 100%, and stop when it is reverted). No one read the code or reproduced the ZeroDivisionError, so the specific faulty calculation has not been identified.

The flag provider's history showed one recent change, which was assumed to be the rollout of monthly-spend-feature. It was not independently verified who made it, when it was scheduled, or whether it was intended to be a full rollout.

The change-event lookup covered only the 236 minutes before 23:56 and returned nothing. It was assumed that no relevant deploy exists outside that window; a faulty change shipped earlier and merely exposed by the flag was considered but never checked.
The pre-existing UpstreamTimeout errors on the account page (present at roughly baseline levels before 23:50) were assumed to be unrelated background noise, not a contributing factor.

Recovery was judged from a single check showing the service at baseline ten seconds after the revert. Baseline was assumed to be the pre-23:55 error level seen in the logs; no longer soak period was observed.

The incident start was placed at 23:56 from per-minute metrics, but a partial rollout at 23:55 (4 of 200 evaluations on) already produced one ZeroDivisionError, so a small amount of customer impact likely began a minute earlier.
Reverting the flag is assumed to be a complete mitigation. The defective code path is still present in the running service and would fail again if the flag were re-enabled.
input.executive_summary: Shortly before midnight UTC on 13/14 September, a new billing-related feature was switched on for all customers of the online shop. The feature contained a latent bug that caused the account page to fail outright for a substantial share of the people who loaded it. Failures began at about 23:56 and an alert fired at 00:01. An automated responder investigated, identified the newly enabled feature as the cause, switched it back off at 00:01:55, and confirmed the service was back to its normal behaviour by 00:02:06. Customers who visited the account page in that roughly six-minute window would have seen errors; other parts of the shop were unaffected, and no data was lost. Impact on orders and revenue was measured separately from the shop's own takings and is reported elsewhere — the figures are not re-derived here. The feature remains off pending a fix to the faulty calculation.
input.root_cause: The feature flag `monthly-spend-feature` was rolled out on io-shop from off to fully on between roughly 23:55 and 23:56 on 13 Sep, and the code path it enabled threw ZeroDivisionError while rendering the account page, so account page requests began failing as soon as the flag reached full traffic. No deploy or release was recorded on the service in the 236 minutes before the incident window, so the flag flip — not a code push — is what changed; the underlying division-by-zero defect was already in the shipped binary and was merely gated by the flag.
